questions.q: What happens if a module references var.resource_group_name but never declares a matching variable block?
options: Terraform silently treats it as an empty string
terraform init fails, since every var reference needs a corresponding variable block somewhere in that module
Terraform automatically creates the variable with a null default
It is ignored unless the output references it too
questions.explain: Every var.* reference inside a module must correspond to a declared variable block in that same module.

questions.q: What is the effect of giving a module's variable block a default value?
options: It becomes required instead of optional
Callers can omit that variable entirely when calling the module
It can no longer be overridden by a caller
It changes the variable's type automatically
questions.explain: A variable with a default is optional for the caller; one without a default is required.

questions.q: Which part of a module is reachable from outside it?
options: Every resource and local value defined anywhere inside the module
Only values explicitly declared in output blocks
Only the first resource block in the module's main.tf
Whatever the caller names when calling the module
questions.explain: Only declared outputs are visible to the caller; anything not output stays internal to the module, by design.

questions.q: What is the correct syntax for reading a module's output elsewhere in the configuration?
options: output.<module name>.<output name>
module.<module name>.<output name>
var.<module name>.<output name>
<module name>.output(<output name>)
questions.explain: module.<name>.<output> reads a module's output value, the same way a resource attribute reference works.

questions.q: In the plan output, why does storage_account_name on the Function App show as "(known after apply)"?
options: Because the Function App resource has a syntax error
Because Terraform refuses to plan resources that depend on modules
Because the value depends on a module output whose resource hasn't been created yet, so the exact value isn't known until apply runs
Because storage_account_name is an invalid argument
questions.explain: Terraform knows the dependency exists but can't know the module's output value before the module's resource is actually created during apply.
